subject: [PATCH] btrfs: write-protect folios during data writeback

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the patch missed zoned cases, but after reevaluation, the code looks good and the issue is covered by lock_delalloc_folios()
reviews.raw_body:
Oh I forgot zoned cases. In that case indeed lock_delalloc_folios() is 
the location that covers all.

Then the code looks good to me now.

Thanks,
Qu

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that two paths, compression and zoned write, lock a delalloc range covering part of a folio, causing issues when calling folio_clear_dirty_for_io() for all folios inside the range, as it would leave the tailing folio's remaining part unwritten. He expressed concerns about the complexity of per-block dirty tracking and suggested that there is a lot of work to be done before existing technical debts can be resolved.
reviews.raw_body:
This involves a lot of technical debts, the main reason is that we have 
two paths that can writeback part of a folio:

- Compression
   AKA, the async submission.

   I had a series converting it to regular submission, but still under
   review, and the current version is still a little complex on the
   OE handling part.

- Zoned write
   I have no idea why we have to do it in the first place.
   I believe WDC people hit some problems with the regular writeback
   path.

The above two paths all lock a delalloc range that can cover part of the 
tailing folio.

If we call folio_clear_dirty_for_io() for all folios inside the range, 
then the tailing folio will not got its remaining part written back, 
because the folio is no longer dirty.

That's why we have to do all the complex per-block dirty tracking, and 
only call folio_clear_dirty_for_io() when there is no dirty block left 
in a folio.

But as Boris pointed out, the delayed timing is already problematic. And 
the current solution is the manual folio_mkclean() calls.

So I'm afraid there are a lot of work to do before we can get rid of the 
existing technical debts.

Thanks,
Qu

2026-07-10.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where, due to a recent change in the Btrfs kernel module, folios (large blocks of data) are not being properly write-protected during data writeback operations. This can lead to corruption and bugs when processes try to modify sectors while they're being used by writeback. The patch reintroduces the necessary write-protection mechanism without dropping the dirty flag on the folio, which would cause other issues. It also adds a debug warning to help prevent similar regressions in the future.
